audience.text: C++ developers building desktop, server, or embedded applications that require PDF processing without external runtime dependencies.

capabilities.text: Open existing PDFs, including password-protected ones, and save changes with incremental metadata updates or full round-trips.
capabilities.title: Open and edit PDF documents

capabilities.text: Extract full text via TextAbsorber or render pages to PNG, JPEG, BMP, or TIFF images using dedicated device classes.
capabilities.title: Extract text and render pages

capabilities.text: Apply AES-256, AES-128, RC4-128, or RC4-40 encryption with granular Permissions flags, and sign with detached PKCS#7 using PdfFileSignature.
capabilities.title: Encrypt and sign documents

capabilities.text: Build documents with positioned text, tables, vector shapes, watermarks, annotations, AcroForm fields, and outlines using the Core API.
capabilities.title: Create PDFs from scratch

capabilities.text: Add and flatten interactive AcroForm fields (TextBoxField, CheckboxField, etc.) and support multiple annotation subtypes with appearance streams.
capabilities.title: Manage forms and annotations

capabilities.text: Read and write document metadata via DocumentInfo and XMP via Metadata, and manage hierarchical outlines and named destinations.
capabilities.title: Access metadata and outlines

limitations.text: Standard-14 font fallback covers 12 of 14 fonts; Symbol and ZapfDingbats lack bundled fallback.
XmpValue type-checking helpers (IsDateTime, IsField, etc.) always return false; use IsString/IsInteger/IsDouble/IsArray instead.
Setting metadata on a from-scratch document and saving throws because there is no existing /Info object to patch.
Permissions set via encryption are enforced by the consuming PDF viewer, not by the library itself.

problems_solved.text: Enables reading, editing, and saving PDF documents in pure C++20 without linking to any third-party PDF libraries or commercial stacks.
Provides text extraction, page rendering, encryption, and form handling through a consistent API mirroring Aspose.PDF for .NET.
Supports building PDFs from scratch with text, tables, vector graphics, annotations, and interactive forms using a single-header interface.

product_summary.text: Aspose.PDF FOSS for C++ is a free, open-source C++20 library for creating, editing, and extracting content from PDF documents with no runtime dependencies.

uncertainties: The exact set of supported annotation subtypes beyond those listed in examples is unclear.
Whether PdfFileSignature supports timestamping or only basic detached PKCS#7 is not stated.
The behavior of TextDevice encoding options beyond UTF-8/UTF-16LE/UTF-16BE/Latin-1/Windows-1252 is unspecified.
Whether embedded files via EmbeddedFiles support arbitrary MIME types is not confirmed.
The scope of Facades API completeness compared to commercial Aspose.PDF for .NET is not quantified.
Whether the library supports PDF/A or PDF/UA conformance is not stated.
The exact CMake target names for linking (e.g., Aspose_PDF_FOSS::aspose_pdf_foss) are not listed.
Whether the library supports incremental updates for already encrypted documents is not stated.

workflows.name: Open and inspect PDF
workflows.text: Load a PDF file, check encryption status, read metadata, and count pages using Document, DocumentInfo, and PageCollection.

workflows.name: Extract text and images
workflows.text: Use TextAbsorber to walk the document or a single page and retrieve text, or use PngDevice/JpegDevice/BmpDevice/TiffDevice to render pages to images.

workflows.name: Encrypt and sign
workflows.text: Apply encryption with AES-256 or RC4 variants using Document::Encrypt and granular Permissions flags, or sign with PdfFileSignature.

workflows.name: Build document from scratch
workflows.text: Create a new Document, add pages, insert text via TextBuilder, draw shapes with Drawing::Graph, and embed tables, annotations, or forms.
